task.description:
Implement ISS-102 per design artefact src/design/iss102-tasks-claimed-by.md.

Requirement summary (from docs/requirements/BPM_Architecture_Backlog.20260611.md §ISS-102):

Acceptance criteria:
1. Migration adds tasks.claimed_by UUID NULL (migration 082_iss102_tasks_claimed_by.sql)
2. POST /tasks/:id/claim performs:
   UPDATE … SET claimed_by=$worker WHERE task_id=$id AND claimed_by IS NULL AND status='PENDING'
   0 rows → 409 Conflict
3. Only claimed_by (or a USER-assigned assignee_ref) may complete the task
4. Partial indexes added: unclaimed-pool index and claimed_by (my tasks) index

Steps:
1. Read design artefact fully
2. Write migrations/082_iss102_tasks_claimed_by.sql - idempotent, additive migration
3. Update src/tasks/store.zig - claim function using new UPDATE pattern, completion guard
4. Update src/api/routes/tasks.zig - claim route returning 409 on double-claim
5. Run: zig build (must exit 0)
6. Run: zig build test (must exit 0)
7. Run: zig build migrate (must exit 0)
8. Check error sets: zig build 2>&1 | grep -i 'error set' (must be empty)
9. Commit to feature/WF02-iss102-20260611 and push
acceptance_criteria: tasks.claimed_by UUID NULL column in migration
Both partial indexes present in migration
Claim endpoint uses claimed_by IS NULL AND status=PENDING guard
Completion checks claimed_by or USER-assigned assignee_ref
No error-set output from zig build stderr

result.summary: ISS-102 implemented: migration 082_iss102_tasks_claimed_by.sql adds claimed_by UUID NULL column and two partial indexes; store.zig adds ClaimError error set and claimTask function with conditional UPDATE + diagnostic SELECT; handleClaim route added to tasks.zig (POST /tasks/:id/claim → 200/404/409/503); handleComplete Step 3 updated to claimed_by-based guard (removes broken group-membership path); serializeTaskDetail updated with claimed_by field; claim route wired in main.zig. zig build, zig build test, zig build migrate all exit 0; no error-set output.

issues.description: Migration uses CREATE INDEX (without CONCURRENTLY) instead of CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY as specified in the design. CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a BEGIN/COMMIT transaction block, which is how the migration runner executes each migration. Regular CREATE INDEX is functionally equivalent; the difference is only that CONCURRENTLY avoids a table-level lock during index creation on a live database. On a dev/test database this is acceptable.
